PAR.title: PAR · word and syllable
PAR.body: The wave-like sign aligns with par in the related cipher’s “messe par monsieur de Bourges” and its contemporary decipherment. In these letters it supplies PAR both on its own and inside words: PAR + L + E + R gives parler.

refs.label: BnF fr. 3984, f. 185 · decipherment, “messe par monsieur de Bourges”

images.caption: Cipher: PAR, followed by MONSIEUR and DE.
Readable copy: “… messe par monsieur de Bourges …”.
Frachetta, line 8: PAR + L + E + R.

ET.title: ET · “and”
ET.body: This dedicated sign supplies et. The related Lisieux cipher has it in the passage rendered “nous en serions mieux et …” in its contemporary decipherment; the same form recurs throughout both letters.

images.caption: The ET occurrence in the related cipher.

MAISTRE.title: Mᵉ → maistre
MAISTRE.body: An M-like base with a raised e is expanded as maistre, modern maître (“master”). The contraction recurs after son twice in Frachetta and after mon in Aldobrandini; the intervening letters are supplied by abbreviation expansion.

images.caption: Frachetta · line 7
Frachetta · line 30
Aldobrandini · recto line 42

PARTICULIER.title: Particulier · abbreviation
PARTICULIER.body: The compact PAR-based abbreviation is expanded using its repeated contexts and the related f. 176v/f. 177v cipher–decipherment pair, which writes out particulier. Querelle calls for the feminine particulière; the compact strokes do not spell every expanded letter.

images.caption: Frachetta · querelle particulière.
Frachetta · de particulier.

MONSIEUR.title: Monsieur · title sign
MONSIEUR.body: Labelled cipher–decipherment comparisons associate a left-bending upper stem with Monsieur. Fifteen labelled title occurrences were checked across two correspondence packets; the local sentence also guides the expansion. A title code supplies the designation, not its letter-by-letter spelling.

images.caption: Upper-stem comparison, with the titles supplied by the readable copies.

SA SAINTETE.body: Labelled cipher–decipherment comparisons associate a right-bending upper stem with Sa Sainteté, “His Holiness”. Fifteen labelled title occurrences were checked across two correspondence packets; the local sentence also guides the expansion. A title code supplies the designation, not its letter-by-letter spelling.

NAUARRE.title: Navarre · word sign
NAUARRE.body: The matching sign aligns with Navarre in the Lisieux decipherment: “Navarre fit sa profession de foy”. The cipher continues FIST SA PRO…, fixing the correspondence independently of the target sentence.

images.caption: The related cipher sign and the Frachetta occurrence.
Readable copy: “Navarre fit sa profession de foy”.

MAYENNE.title: Mayenne · word sign
MAYENNE.body: Six aligned occurrences in the Lisieux packet support the Mayenne designation. The illustrated readable passage names Mayenne in a request for direct papal communication; the code gives the person, while the expanded title is editorial.

images.caption: The related cipher passage.
Its readable copy, naming Mayenne.

ROY D ESPAGNE.title: Roy d’Espagne · word sign
ROY D ESPAGNE.body: The looped sign aligns with “le Roy d’Espaigne” in f. 188 and its decipherment on f. 184. An earlier interlinear gloss corroborates the King of Spain reading; exact expanded spelling and articles are editorial.

images.caption: Target, matching cipher and readable King-of-Spain designation.

GUISE.title: Guise · word sign
GUISE.body: The related cipher places the same loop after MARIER; its readable copy names “Mons de Guise” before “avec l’Infante”. Those matching flanks establish the name; the forename and exact title are contextual expansions.

refs.label: BnF fr. 3984, f. 176 · MARIER + name sign

images.caption: The matching loop and the written-out Guise in the readable copy.

PAPE.title: Pape · word sign
PAPE.body: Earlier manuscripts write pape above this lambda-like sign: three glossed occurrences in two letters, including “au feu pape Gregoire”. The target repeats it before GREGOIRE.

images.caption: The interlinear PAPE gloss in an earlier letter.

INFANTE.title: Infante · word sign
INFANTE.body: The two-topped sign after AVEC in f. 176 aligns with l’Infante in its readable copy on f. 177. The same sign appears in Aldobrandini’s marriage clause, giving the Infanta designation.

images.caption: Cipher: AVEC followed by the Infante sign.
Readable copy: the Guise–Infante marriage passage.

LE LÉGAT.title: Le légat · word sign
LE LÉGAT.body: The g-like sign aligns with le légat in the related cipher and its readable copy. The nearby Monsieur sign is separate; légat is an office, subsequently identified from the historical setting as Filippo Sega.

refs.label: BnF fr. 3984, f. 176v · cipher, Monsieur + légat

images.caption: Aldobrandini, line 35: separate MONSIEUR and LÉGAT signs.

QUAND.title: Quand / quant · contextual expansion
QUAND.body: The same arrow introduces a concession in line 18 and a change of topic in line 23. Together these support quand / quant à. Henry IV’s letters supply period parallels; this assignment rests on context across occurrences, rather than an independently labelled codebook entry.

refs.label: Henry IV, Lettres missives III, printed p. 125

images.caption: Frachetta · line 18.
Frachetta · line 23.

Vostre Seigneurie Illustrissime.title: V. S. I. · courtesy abbreviation
Vostre Seigneurie Illustrissime.body: The initials expand to Vostre Seigneurie Illustrissime, “Your Most Illustrious Lordship”. The letter also gives the title in ordinary handwriting and in its closing; the expansion supplies the abbreviated letters.

images.caption: The abbreviated courtesy in the cipher text.

SAINT.title: S[ainc]t → saint
SAINT.body: The contracted S…t is expanded as sainct, modern saint, in Saint-Siège. The brackets identify supplied abbreviation letters; siege is written separately.

images.caption: The Saint abbreviation before SIEGE.

5ᶜ = cinq cens (500).title: 5ᶜ → cinq cens
5ᶜ = cinq cens (500).body: The raised c multiplies 5 by one hundred. The following MIL supplies another factor of 1,000, giving 500,000 écus. Cinq cens expands a number; it is not a sequence of individually enciphered letters.

images.caption: The quantity before MIL ESCUS.
